Hello fellow labbers! I have a HP smart array P410i raid controller w/ 512MB BBWC, hooked up to a SSD and couple of HDDs. The SSD and one of the HDD is for VM storage. The controller is set to 0%/100% read/write. (For some reason if I set the array to 50/50, large sequential read plummets on my CIFS share.)

After doing a little researching, I found Best Practice Usage for SSD Hard Drives on HP SmartArray Controllers written by HP. In it, it says if I have 512MB or bigger BBWC, SSD write cache should not be enabled and set the Smart Array controller for 70%/30% read/write.

I'm still noob at this, so I'm not sure if I want to leave the write cache as-is or change it to HP's recommendation. Does anyone have any experience changing the write cache scheme? What are the performance implications of disabling SSD write cache?
Enable write cache for SSD on raid controller?

Too many caches can be bad for performance. In your cache your controller has cache, your SSD has and the SSD is the cache for the file system. The cache on the SSD is most likely smaller than the 512MB of the controller, so it possibly only slows things down. It's one small cache between two bigger ones, that's a performance killer.

That's theory, use benchmarks to see which configuration fits your use case best. Maybe it's faster to shut off the cache of the controller and let the SSD handle it. But both at once is not a good idea.
Thanks! Since I'm using ESXi, I guess I can use the reporting from there to figure out whether performance degrades or not.
